_comment: Tutor LLM candidates. Swapping models is a continuous process, so it is a
registry plus two commands rather than a procedure:
make model-use NAME=qwen3-1.7b     # fetch if needed, restart, verify
make model-check                   # accuracy + perf against the running one
Which model is live is machine-local (deploy/.env, gitignored) — the bench
and a device may legitimately differ. The default lives in the compose file.
Swapping the TUTOR model does not affect retrieval; that is the embed model.
So the regression here is behaviour and speed, and `make eval` is unchanged.

models.name: qwen3-1.7b
models.notes: Shipped in v0.4/v0.5. Measured 49.5 tok/s prefill, 9.9 decode. Passes all accuracy cases.

models.name: qwen3-0.6b
models.notes: KNOWN BAD, kept deliberately. ~5.0s loop but answers yes to yes/no questions regardless of the lesson, and invents facts. model-check MUST fail on this one — if it passes, the harness is broken, not the model.

models.name: lfm2.5-1.2b
models.notes: Jenya's recommendation. Reported on Pi 5: 71 tok/s prefill, 15 decode, against our 49.5/9.9 — projects ~1.8s off a grounded turn. URL deliberately left blank rather than guessed: fill it with `make model-add NAME=lfm2.5-1.2b URL=... FILE=...` once the GGUF repo path is confirmed. It sits between the model that fails the accuracy cases and the one that passes, so run model-check before believing 'similar quality'.
